deep.reconstruction:
No mathematics on this page. It continues Riemann's excerpt notes from Herbart, which began on the previous page with the heading 'Herbart Bd. V. p. 501, §. 102. Unterschied des Geistigen und Leiblichen'. The source is almost certainly Herbart's Lehrbuch zur Psychologie, §§102–103, in the Hartenstein edition of the Werke. The text is in Riemann's hand but is mostly copied or paraphrased Herbart, not Riemann's own argument.

(1) The opening sentence finishes the source/spring metaphor. A spring is the natural symbol of the mental, though it is really passive. Imagination merely lends it the appearance of something inside that strains to lift and push the water.

(2) Causality in everyday speech: 'das kommt daher' means 'this here is the effect of that cause there'. Common sense dimly feels a contradiction: one that would arise in the affected thing if it had changed itself. Herbart's doctrine is that self-change is contradictory. In feeling this, common sense goes further than the (Kantian?) school, which oddly found in the concept of causality nothing but the rule of a sequence.

(3) A second circumstance leads to the assumption of an external world. Riemann has inserted '(Raum)' above the line, flagging the passage as relevant to space. That circumstance is human mobility within one's surroundings. Without mobility, the intuitions of things would be taken for the things themselves.

Because one distinguishes absent from present, one learns that appearing or not appearing is accidental to objects. Objects keep their places in the gradually forming, ordering and connecting series of representations, even when the sequence of intuitions changes.

Their appearing (visibility, audibility) is ascribed to them as a kind of radiation sphere whose strength diminishes with distance. The objects themselves are taken as the source of the appearing. The centre where the rays of appearing converge and cross from all sides grounds the Ich.

The Ich also needs the inner world to develop. Moving about amid the outer world (the Nicht-Ich), it does not merely absorb and terminate rays but sends out rays of its own, by which it moves what resists. Hence one cannot say whether the Ich is more active or passive; almost always both occur, in unequal measure.

The only quasi-mathematical content is the qualitative image of an intensity that decreases with distance. It is not quantified.

results.what: Excerpt of Herbart's psychological account of causality and of how mobility leads to the notions of external world and space (Ich as convergence point of 'rays of appearing'); Riemann marks the passage '(Raum)'
results.modern_name: Herbartian associationist epistemology / genetic psychology of spatial representation

deep.surprise_reason: Reading notes copied or paraphrased from Herbart, with no mathematics. Riemann's study of Herbart and his interest in Herbart's genesis of spatial representation are well documented: he called himself a Herbartian in psychology and epistemology, and the Habilitationsvortrag cites Herbart.
transcription_corrections: '(Raum)' is a superscript insertion by Riemann above 'Außenwelt', flagging the passage as relevant to space.
'der mir mit unserer Nothwendigkeit zur Außenwelt' likely reads 'der uns mit einer (Art von) Nothwendigkeit zur Außenwelt hinüberleiten mußte/möchte'.

'als den Anfang[?] einer Ruhe[?]' is likely 'als die Regel einer Reihe/Folge', referring to the Kantian view of causality as a rule of succession. The underlined word before 'Schule' is probably 'kantische'.
'der in dem Wandern[?] entstehen[?] wäre' is probably 'der in dem Leidenden entstanden wäre' (the contradiction of self-change).
'Die Gegenstände erkennen[?], so fern sie nahe stehen, auch nach Plänen[?]' is uncertain. It possibly reads 'Die Gegenstände behalten ... ihre Plätze in seinen ... Vorstellungsreihen'.
'wenn die Reihenfolge der Anschauungen [?] wird' probably has a verb such as 'unterbrochen/gewechselt'.
'schnell aufgefunden[?] im Begriff ist' is uncertain. It possibly reads 'Quell und Ursprung ... ist'.
The word 'Gegenwärtigen' is struck through before 'Abwesenden'. The transcription's bracketing is correct in spirit.
